provenance: Lane split derived by the orchestrator applying the Stage-2 decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) because the decision-agent run was interrupted by a session rate limit. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — load of a known-good AV filter driver on a host that does not run that AV product, or driver hash/signature-context mismatch, is a discrete hunt signal (Sysmon EID 6)

medium — SharePoint/IIS exploitation is detectable via WAF/IPS signatures for CVE-2019-0604 and anomalous web-worker child processes (w3wp.exe spawning cmd.exe), though n-day exploitation can precede the first host artifact

medium — new/modified webshell files in IIS web-content directories and web-worker processes spawning shells are detectable via file-integrity monitoring and process-lineage analytics, though masquerade-as-server-file naming defeats simple name rules

medium — unexpected modules/handlers or unmanaged HTTP.sys URL reservations on an IIS server are detectable via IIS module auditing and URL-ACL review, though the implants deliberately bind below the IIS/HTTP-API layer

detection_candidates.technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — new service/driver registration and service-config-change events (Event ID 7045/7040) on a server are discrete signals, though driver installs blend with legitimate admin activity

medium — anomalous internal RDP (Event ID 4624 type 10 / 4778) from a server or newly-active source, and RDP sessions correlated to a compromised web host, are detectable via authentication and session telemetry
medium — runtime decode-then-execute is partly observable via AMSI/.NET in-memory content, though the memory-resident server-side design leaves little host telemetry

medium — malicious driver loads are detectable via kernel-module-load telemetry (Sysmon EID 6), Microsoft vulnerable/blocked-driver policy, and signature/hash review, though a loaded kernel rootkit can then subvert host visibility

detection_candidates.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Windows Event Log
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — stop/kill of the EventLog service and gaps in event-log continuity are detectable via service-state monitoring (Event ID 7035/7036, 1100) and log-continuity analytics, though the technique is quiet by design

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — a server web/host process spawning cmd.exe is detectable via process-lineage analytics where interactive shells are abnormal, though cmd usage is ubiquitous
medium — internal scanning bursts (many connections/short-lived sessions from one source) are detectable via network flow analytics, though scanning can be low-and-slow

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — capability development is off-victim; the shared tooling family is an attribution/triage hunting signal, not a host detection

low — the defining hunt case: no outbound beacon exists to catch, and inbound triggers ride legitimate web ports; hunt via HTTP.sys URL-reservation/UrlGroup review, unexpected IOCTL-consuming drivers, and memory scanning of web-server processes

low — C2 is inbound-only, TLS-wrapped, and rides ports 80/443 with no beacon; hunt via anomalous request patterns to server endpoints and HTTP.sys-level listener enumeration rather than signature detection
low — driver-level IOCTL command channels produce essentially no standard network telemetry; only reachable via kernel/driver behavioral analysis and memory forensics
low — proxying rides the compromised server's own web channel; hunt via anomalous internal connections sourced from a web/edge server rather than a discrete signature
low — tunnelled remote-access traffic is wrapped inside the compromised host's normal channels; hunt via traffic-timing/volume anomalies and unexpected internal RDP paths
low — the custom crypto layer sits inside otherwise-normal HTTPS; hunt via YARA on the shared encryption constants in samples, not log detection

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Software Packing
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — packing/obfuscation defeats static AV signatures; hunt via obfuscator-artifact YARA and in-memory behavioral analysis

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — encoding/encryption at rest defeats static inspection; hunt via entropy analysis and decoded in-memory content rather than log detection
low — reflective/in-memory loading avoids disk artifacts and masks execution within legitimate server processes; hunt via in-memory scanning and CLR/shellcode-load anomalies
low — kernel-assisted injection into privileged processes is largely invisible to user-mode EDR; hunt via kernel-callback/driver-behavior telemetry and memory forensics
low — kernel-level privilege escalation via signed/repurposed drivers is difficult to observe from user mode; hunt via driver-load provenance and kernel behavioral analysis
low — driver-enforced file protection operates in kernel and resists user-mode inspection; hunt via presence of the AV filter driver on non-AV hosts and files that resist deletion/modification

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — name/location masquerading defeats name-based allow-lists; hunt via signer/hash validation and original-filename metadata mismatch
low — impairment is achieved via kernel-mode file protection and passive design rather than noisy tool-killing; hunt via driver provenance and AV/EDR tamper-attempt telemetry
low — native-API/IOCTL calls are ubiquitous and hard to distinguish; only reachable via targeted driver/behavioral instrumentation
low — file transfers arrive inbound to a passive listener and are often loaded straight into memory; hunt via correlating listener activity with new file writes/assembly loads
low — file reads by a server process are routine; collection blends with the passive C2 and produces little discrete telemetry
low — exfiltration rides the passive-listener response channel and blends with normal web responses; the inbound-only design limits egress visibility
